name: Samhallsbyggnadsbolaget I Norden AB
reason: Distressed Swedish property owner: FFO/share collapsed from SEK 2.12 (2021) to -0.30 (2023) and 0.60 (2025) with net debt/EBITDA of 56x, 79%/yr share-count growth and acquisitions at 2.75x FCF, so the balance sheet fails the recession test.

name: BFF Bank S.p.A.
reason: Italian factoring of public-administration receivables whose profits lean on late-payment interest and rates; adjusted EPS of EUR 0.81 (2025) is below the 0.98 peak, adjusted runs 53% above GAAP on average, consensus is -22% for FY1, and the Bank of Italy supervisory findings add regulatory risk.

name: Stellantis N.V.
reason: Cyclical auto OEM: adjusted EPS swung from EUR 6.42 (2023) to -0.42 (2025) with EBIT margin from 12.1% to -14.5%, and the EV transition and US tariffs make 5-10 year earnings unforecastable.

name: Atos Group
reason: Restructured IT-services group: EPS went from EUR 575 (2019) to losses in 2021, 2022 and 2025 after a debt-for-equity swap, the share count grew 30%/yr over 10 years, average ROIC is -12%, and revenue shrank 2.9%/yr.

name: 3i Group plc
reason: EPS (GBP 0.85 to 5.39, 20% 10y CAGR, 22% average ROE) is mainly fair-value gains on a portfolio dominated by Action; Action is a special discount retailer, but reported earnings track its valuation multiple and one asset, so they cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Navios Maritime Partners LP
reason: Dry-bulk, container and tanker shipowner whose earnings are set by charter rates: EPS went from USD -2.42 (2019) to 15.75 (2021) and 9.94 (2025), with acquisitions at 1.9x FCF and an 18%/yr share-count increase.

name: Aroundtown SA
reason: Leveraged German office/hotel landlord: FFO/share fell from EUR 0.36 (2018) to 0.26 (2025), net debt/EBITDA is 16.9x, average ROE is 9%, and consensus long-term growth is negative, so it fails both the growth and balance-sheet tests.

name: Shawbrook Group Plc
reason: UK SME and specialist property lender, re-listed in 2025 under private-equity control: EPS of GBP 0.35 (2025) is 18% below 2024 with a patchy record (6 years of data), 15% average ROE and credit-cycle exposure; consensus 10-14% is plausible but unproven through a downturn.

name: Webuild SpA
reason: Large-project contractor with an EBIT margin averaging -1.2% (10-year max 3.9%), 0.8% average ROIC, adjusted EPS running 299% above GAAP and a 7%/yr share-count increase; this is cheap-but-ordinary contracting with no moat.

name: Kruk S.A.
reason: Founder-led CEE debt purchaser with a strong record (EPS PLN 15.69 in 2017 to 55.07 in 2025, 22% average ROE), but net debt/EBITDA is 4.65x, growth depends on debt-funded portfolio purchases priced against the credit cycle, and earnings include collection-curve revaluations; consensus is 5.5-12%.

name: TBC Bank Group Plc
reason: Georgia's leading bank: adjusted EPS of GEL 5.9 (2016) to 24.96 (2025) grew through the low-rate years with 22.7% average ROE and 10.8-15.9% consensus, but Georgian political/sanctions risk, the GEL exposure and the Uzbekistan digital expansion make 5-10 year forecasts unreliable.

name: Danaos Corporation
reason: Containership lessor whose earnings follow the charter cycle: EPS fell from USD 20.30 (2015) to 7.18 (2020), peaked at 34.68 (2022) and was 26.28 in 2025, and the 10-year EPS CAGR is 2.6% with FY2 consensus -4.5%.

name: Banca IFIS S.p.A.
reason: Italian factoring and NPL bank in a transformational integration of its 2025 illimity takeover (consensus EPS -70% FY1 then +103% FY2); EPS of EUR 1.87 (2015) to 3.19 (2025) is only a 5.5% CAGR, with a -82% year in 2020 and 6.1% average ROIC.

name: Paragon Banking Group PLC
reason: UK buy-to-let lender with a good record (EPS GBP 0.35 to 1.10, 12.2% CAGR, shares -4%/yr) but at a peak-NIM EPS high; it is not through-cycle best-in-class (13.1% average ROE), and FY1-FY2 consensus of only 2.6%/4.5% fails the US bank standard.

name: OSB Group PLC
reason: UK specialist mortgage lender: EPS of GBP 0.76 (2025) is below the 1.00 peak of 2022, with a 5y CAGR of 5.4%, a -25% year in 2023 (EIR/refinancing behaviour) and FY1 consensus of -2.6%; this is ordinary rate- and credit-cycle lending.

name: Credit Agricole SA
reason: Listed arm of the mutual Credit Agricole group (about 62% owned by the regional banks via SAS Rue la Boetie): average ROE is 7.5% (below the 10% bank bar), the 10y EPS CAGR is 6.2% to an EUR 2.18 peak, and FY2-FY3 consensus is 6.6-9.2%.

name: TAURON Polska Energia S.A.
reason: State-controlled, coal-heavy Polish utility: EBIT margin is at its 10-year high (14.4%, 100th pctile), EPS swung from PLN -1.41 (2020) to 1.78 (2025) with FY1 consensus -17%, average ROE is 3.2%, and tariffs and decarbonisation are set by government policy.

name: Investec plc
reason: UK/South African specialist bank and wealth manager: EPS of GBP 0.81 is at a peak after the rate cycle (2019 -59%), revenue CAGR is 3.7%, average ROE is 11.2%, and earnings depend on SA/UK rates and investment-banking activity.

name: Molten Ventures PLC
reason: Venture-capital investment trust whose earnings are unrealised valuation marks: EPS of GBP -1.59 (2022), 0.00 (2024) and 0.69 (2025), 15.7%/yr share-count growth and negative FCF; earnings are set by capital markets.

name: Reinet Investments S.C.A.
reason: Rupert-family-controlled investment holding (Pension Insurance Corporation, BAT stake and funds) whose EPS is fair-value moves (EUR -34.92 in 2019, 96.50 in 2020, -12.82 in 2022), with adjusted EPS far from GAAP and the PIC sale reducing it to a cash/portfolio vehicle.
